title: Pinned-base portal frame with a load at midspan of the beam - values printed by the vendor that do not reproduce

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: Timoshenko, Strength of Materials, Part I, 2nd ed. 1940, pp. 188-191 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Plane problem in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held; in-plane bending about local z. Portal: columns 100 in high, 2 in x 2 in (A = 4 in^2, I = 1.3333 in^4), beam of 120 in, 2 in wide and 4 in deep (A = 8 in^2, I = 10.667 in^4), E = 30e6 psi, pinned bases; 1000 lb at midspan (taken downward; the page's listing applies it upward, its results are magnitudes). First-order analysis with axial deformation, without shear deformation. Same model as problem 'portal-pinned-midspan-load' (whose recomputed targets are active); the targets here are the vendor's printed values only.

targets.precisionNote: printed "2754.97"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; moment at the ends of the beam; value of the page's closed-form expression
targets.sign: the page prints a magnitude; sign from the reference solution, engine convention (docs/CONVENTIONS.md)

quarantine.diagnosis: Missed by 2.3e-5 relative (13 times the tolerance): engine -2755.035 lb in, printed 2,754.97. The page's value comes from a closed-form expression that neglects axial deformation, evaluated on the page with rounded section properties (it prints I = 10.67 and 1.333 in^4 and '= 2,754 in-lb' next to the formula, 2,754.97 in its table). The same expression with the exact properties (I_b / I_c = 8) gives 2755.10 lb in; the frame of the statement, with axial deformation, gives 2755.03 lb in (reference program of verification/derive/vendor_reference.py = engine to 1e-9). The printed digits beyond the fourth are not significant. The page's other two values (500 and 27.55 lb) reproduce and are targets of the active problem.
